text:
taylor: Quick sync - we've started seeing HQ customers sending an `X-Embed-Estimate` header from a new Go SDK. Some big requests are being routed to the conservative pipeline and it spikes token cost. Can we align on semantics + how console should expose it?

rachel: What does the header contain? dims? tokens? a byte estimate?

taylor: It's meant to be a client-side token estimate (int) for better batching. Example: `X-Embed-Estimate: 120`. But older clients sometimes send `X-Embed-Estimate: 120,240` for multi-inputs.

jin: That's dangerous. Our router expects single scalar estimate to pick fast-path that depends on GPU batching budget. If it gets a csv it fails parse and we fallback to the safe queue.

marcus: Can you paste an ingress log showing the parse behaviour?

taylor: from ingress-proxy on canary:
```
2026-03-20T09:02:11Z ERROR ingress.parse: X-Embed-Estimate malformed "120,240" -> route=conservative, reason=estimate-multi
```

rachel: Do we want to change router to accept CSV and sum them? Or should we treat anything non-scalar as invalid and keep current behaviour?

jin: My vote: keep router conservative. But add tolerant parsing as a debug-mode: if header looks like csv and all ints, compute sum and tag request with `embed.estimate.parsed=sum` so we can measure accuracy. Do not use it for routing until we have telemetry.

taylor: Agreed. Also propose telemetry keys: `ingress.header.embed_estimate.present`, `embed.estimate.parse=(ok|csv|fail)`, `ingress.route.chosen=(fast|conservative|overflow)`, `ingress.estimate.delta_ms` (route decision duration).

marcus: For console, surface a per-tenant "Estimate header adoption" card and an "Estimate parse failures" alert. Add a control: "Accept client estimates" (default OFF). If enabled, router will honor parsed scalar or summed csv.

rachel: UX caveat: toggle default OFF+tooltip: "Enable only if your SDKs send integer token estimates consistently (Go SDK >= v1.9)." Also add a link to guidance on producing accurate estimates.

jin: Rollout plan: 1) Patch canary to emit `embed.estimate.parse` values and not change routing. 2) Collect 72h telemetry. 3) Dogfood in-house services with toggle ON for 48h. 4) 0.5% tenant opt-in for 7 days, watch for: parse_fail_rate > 0.2% OR median latency increase > 10ms OR cost_per_token increase > 2% -> auto-revert.

taylor: Owners: Jin (runtime) + Marcus (console) + DevEx (Go SDK). DevEx already has a PR to normalize header for multi-input requests (they'll send a single-summed estimate or omit header).

ops-bot: New PR: go-sdk@1.9.2 - "normalize X-Embed-Estimate: sum multi-inputs, omit when unknown" -> https://internal.devex/patch/1.9.2

rachel: Add console panels requested:
- per-tenant fast vs conservative route split (timeseries + rolling %).
- estimate parse outcome histogram (ok|csv|fail).
- top 10 tenant SDK versions sending malformed estimates.
- cost delta vs baseline for toggled tenants.

jin: Also add alert rule: `embed.estimate.parse:fail rate > 0.2% over 15m` -> page eng-oncall. And `route.split.change > 10%` over 5m -> page infra.

taylor: Runbook note: If mass fallback observed, steps: 1) turn toggle OFF for affected orgs, 2) enable ingress LB header-stripper for `X-Embed-Estimate`, 3) roll back SDK deployment guidance to customers.

marcus: Console UX question: show raw sample headers? Might be sensitive. Maybe show anonymized samples and counts.

rachel: Yes, anonymized only. Also show recommended SDK versions.

jin: I'll land telemetry patch in canary tonight. Marcus, can you mock console cards by EOD so we can review during dogfood?

taylor: Thanks team. I'll draft the rollout doc and include the gating thresholds/alerts and link to DevEx PR.

ops-bot: Created ticket ENG-embed-estimate-rollout and linked to PRs and canary traces.
